newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors look long term.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors look long term.

text.p: Heavy action in long dated call options on shares of Compaq Computer Corp on the Pacific Stock Exchange and a big trade in a long term option on BankAmerica Corp highlighted individual equity options trading on Tuesday.
The trades, in an otherwise quiet session, suggested investors were selectively looking at longer term potential, traders said.
Other highlights included Philip Morris Cos Inc as the stock continued to recover from its recent battering. Also, a couple Coca-Cola Co options were active.
In late afternoon trading, Compaq was up 1/8 at 56-3/4 on 1.29 million shares. The most active options were the January 1997 50 and 60 calls, which traded 1,404 and 2,849 contracts respectively.
"Some of that was a market maker spread and the seller was the public," said the Compaq specialist on the floor of the Pacific Stock Exchange.
He said investors were probably playing the volatility.
"People are taking a shot at January volatility," he said. "They'll have two earnings reports and it will be after the (U.S. presidential) election."
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said it did not appear that the trading in the two January calls was related.
He added that heavy trading in the Compaq September 60 put on Monday was noteworthy because it pushed that option's open interest sharply higher.
Nearly 17,000 of the September 60 puts traded on Monday, and its open interest increased by 15,327, more than the open interest in any other Compaq option.
The Compaq specialist said that activity on Monday was an institution selling the contracts to the crowd.
The Compaq September 60 put traded nearly 900 contracts on Tuesday. The September 55 put, with open interest of 4,222 through Monday, traded about 850.
The other long term option was a long term equity anticipation security, or LEAP, on BankAmerica Corp.
The BankAmerica January 1998 60 call traded 4,845 contracts, making it the most active call on the CBOE.
The option was up 1/8 at 24-7/8. BankAmerica shares were off 3/4 at 80-5/8.

Elsewhere, the Coca-Cola Co February 1997 50 call also made the actives list on the CBOE, with 2,000 contracts changing hands. The option was unchanged at 4-1/2 and had open interest of 1,692 through Monday.
The Coca-Cola Co November 40 call also was busy, with nearly 2,100 contracts trading. Coke shares gained 3/8 to 51-1/2.
